faq.q: The SVG has no width or height. Will it still convert?
faq.a: Yes. The tool reads the intrinsic size from the width and height attributes if they exist; if they don't, it falls back to the viewBox to work out the proportions, and uses a sensible default only when neither is present. It also understands unit suffixes such as pt and mm and converts them to pixels, and it writes an explicit width/height onto a copy of the SVG so Firefox and Chrome both rasterise it reliably.

faq.q: How do I get a transparent PNG, and what does JPG do with transparency?
faq.a: Choose PNG (or WebP) and transparency is preserved — the preview sits on a checkerboard so you can see exactly which pixels are see-through. JPG has no alpha channel, so picking JPG reveals a background colour picker (white by default) and the transparent areas are filled with that colour before encoding, which avoids the usual black box behind a logo.

faq.q: Can I control the output resolution?
faq.a: Yes. Pick 1×, 2×, 3× or 4× of the SVG's natural size for a quick crisp upscale, or choose 'Exact width (px)' and type the width you need — the height follows the aspect ratio automatically. Because SVG is vector, scaling up stays sharp. The longest side is capped at 8192 px so a huge value can't exhaust your browser's memory.
